title: Leviticus Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 22.

questions.question: To whom did the LORD speak in Leviticus 22:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:1 states that the LORD spake unto Moses.

questions.question: Who were instructed to separate themselves from the holy things to not profane God's name?
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and his sons
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:2 commands Aaron and his sons to separate themselves from the holy things and not profane God's name.

questions.question: What will happen to anyone of Aaron's seed who goes to the holy things with uncleanness upon him?
options: That soul shall be cut off from the LORD's presence
He shall be cleansed and allowed to eat
questions.correctAnswer: That soul shall be cut off from the LORD's presence
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:3 says the soul with uncleanness upon him who goes to the holy things shall be cut off from God's presence.

questions.question: True or False: A leper from the seed of Aaron is allowed to eat of the holy things before he is clean.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:4 says a leper shall not eat of the holy things until he is clean.

questions.question: What must a person do if he touches anything unclean by the dead before eating the holy things?
questions.correctAnswer: Wash his flesh with water
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:6 commands the soul to wash his flesh with water before eating the holy things.

questions.question: When is a person considered clean after touching something unclean, allowing him to eat the holy things?
questions.correctAnswer: When the sun is down
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:7 states that when the sun is down, the person shall be clean and may eat the holy things.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 22:8, what kind of animals shall not be eaten to avoid defiling oneself?
options: Those that die of themselves or are torn by beasts
questions.correctAnswer: Those that die of themselves or are torn by beasts
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:8 forbids eating animals that die of themselves or are torn with beasts to avoid defilement.

questions.question: True or False: Strangers and hired servants are permitted to eat of the holy thing.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:10 states that no stranger, sojourner of the priest, or hired servant shall eat of the holy thing.

questions.question: Who may eat of the priest's meat if the priest buys a soul with his money?
options: The priest and those born in his house
questions.correctAnswer: The priest and those born in his house
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:11 says that if the priest buys any soul, he and those born in his house may eat of his meat.

questions.question: True or False: A priest's daughter married to a stranger may eat of the holy offerings.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:12 states that if the priest's daughter is married to a stranger, she may not eat of the holy offerings.

questions.question: What is required if a man eats of the holy thing unwittingly?
options: He must add a fifth part and give it to the priest
He must offer a burnt offering
He must fast for three days
He must confess to the priest
questions.correctAnswer: He must add a fifth part and give it to the priest
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:14 instructs that if a man eats of the holy thing unwittingly, he shall add a fifth part and give it to the priest.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT allowed to be eaten to avoid bearing iniquity and profaning the holy things?
options: The holy things of the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The holy things of the children of Israel
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:15-16 warns not to profane the holy things or suffer iniquity by eating them improperly.

questions.question: In what order does the chapter instruct the following: 1) Do not eat of the holy things with uncleanness, 2) Do not let strangers eat of the holy things, 3) Wash flesh after touching unclean things.
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:3 commands not to eat the holy things with uncleanness first, then 22:6 commands washing flesh after touching unclean things, followed by 22:10 forbidding strangers to eat.

questions.question: Who is commanded to keep the LORD's ordinances to avoid bearing sin and death?
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and his sons
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:9 instructs Aaron and his sons to keep the ordinances to avoid sin and death.

questions.question: True or False: The soul which touches creeping things and becomes unclean must remain unclean until evening.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:6 says the soul touching such things is unclean until evening.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 22:12, what is the restriction placed on a priest's daughter who marries a stranger?
options: She may not eat of an offering of the holy things
She may eat of the holy things freely
She must offer sacrifices for her husband
She must separate herself from the priest's household
questions.correctAnswer: She may not eat of an offering of the holy things
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:12 states that if the priest's daughter is married to a stranger, she may not eat of an offering of the holy things, showing the importance of lineage and purity in participation.

questions.question: What condition allows a priest's daughter to eat of her father's meat after marriage, according to Leviticus 22:13?
options: If she is a widow or divorced and has no child, returning to her father's house
If she attends the temple regularly
If she offers a sacrifice for her husband
If she remains married to a stranger
questions.correctAnswer: If she is a widow or divorced and has no child, returning to her father's house
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:13 explains that if the priest's daughter is a widow or divorced, has no child, and returns to her father's house as in her youth, she shall eat of her father's meat, but no stranger shall eat of it.

questions.question: What is required of a person who eats of the holy thing unwittingly, as stated in Leviticus 22:14?
options: They must add a fifth part to it and give it to the priest with the holy thing
They must offer a burnt sacrifice
They must fast for three days
They must confess their sin publicly
questions.correctAnswer: They must add a fifth part to it and give it to the priest with the holy thing
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:14 directs that if anyone eats of the holy thing unwittingly, they shall put the fifth part unto it and give it to the priest with the holy thing, emphasizing accountability even in unintentional actions.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Leviticus 22:15-16 for profaning the holy things of the children of Israel?
options: They shall bear sin for it and die
They shall be exiled from Israel
They shall be forgiven after repentance
questions.correctAnswer: They shall bear sin for it and die
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:15-16 warns that profaning the holy things causes the profaner to bear the iniquity of trespass and die, underscoring the sanctity of offerings and God's sanctification of them.

questions.question: Who is allowed to offer burnt offerings to the LORD according to Leviticus 22:18?
options: Anyone of the house of Israel or strangers in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Anyone of the house of Israel or strangers in Israel
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:18 states that any person from the house of Israel or strangers in Israel who will offer oblations for vows or freewill offerings may offer them to the LORD, showing inclusivity in worship.

questions.question: What requirement is given in Leviticus 22:19 for animals offered as burnt offerings?
options: They must be males without blemish
They can be any animal regardless of condition
questions.correctAnswer: They must be males without blemish
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:19 commands offering a male without blemish of the beeves, sheep, or goats for burnt offerings, emphasizing the need for perfection in sacrifices.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 22:20, what happens if an animal offered has a blemish?
options: It shall be accepted with a reduced offering
It shall be accepted only for peace offerings
It shall be accepted after cleansing
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be accepted
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:20 clearly states that any animal with a blemish shall not be offered as it will not be acceptable before the LORD, teaching the importance of offering the best to God.

questions.question: What distinguishes a peace offering from other offerings as per Leviticus 22:21?
options: It must be perfect without blemish to be accepted
It can be offered by non-priests
It must be a female animal
questions.correctAnswer: It must be perfect without blemish to be accepted
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:21 states that peace offerings to accomplish vows or freewill offerings must be perfect without blemish to be accepted, underscoring God's demand for purity in offerings.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions disqualifies an animal from being offered to the LORD according to Leviticus 22:22?
options: Blindness, brokenness, maiming, having a wen, scurvy, or scabbed
Being younger than one year old
questions.correctAnswer: Blindness, brokenness, maiming, having a wen, scurvy, or scabbed
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:22 explicitly forbids offering animals that are blind, broken, maimed, have a wen, scurvy, or scabbed, indicating these defects make the sacrifice unacceptable.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 22:23 differentiate between freewill offerings and vows regarding animals with defects?
options: Animals with defects may be offered for freewill offerings but not for vows
Animals with defects are accepted for both offerings
Animals with defects are rejected for both offerings
Animals with defects are accepted only if the priest allows
questions.correctAnswer: Animals with defects may be offered for freewill offerings but not for vows
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:23 permits animals with superfluous or lacking parts for freewill offerings but not for vows, highlighting the higher standard for vow offerings.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 22:24 prohibit concerning the condition of offerings?
options: Offering bruised, crushed, broken, or cut animals
Offering animals older than three years
questions.correctAnswer: Offering bruised, crushed, broken, or cut animals
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:24 prohibits offering animals that are bruised, crushed, broken, or cut, emphasizing the requirement for offerings to be whole and unblemished.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 22:25 say about offerings from a stranger's hand?
options: They shall not be accepted because of corruption and blemishes
They are accepted if the animal is perfect
They must be inspected by a priest before acceptance
They may be accepted with a special sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not be accepted because of corruption and blemishes
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:25 states that bread or offerings from a stranger's hand with corruption or blemishes shall not be accepted, highlighting the importance of purity in offerings.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 22:27, an animal is acceptable for offering by fire on the altar from the day it is born.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:27 requires that a bullock, sheep, or goat must be seven days under its dam and only from the eighth day onwards is it acceptable for offering by fire, so it is not acceptable from birth.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 22:28, what is the rule regarding killing a cow or ewe and its young?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:28 commands that one shall not kill both a cow or ewe and her young on the same day, showing respect for animal life and family bonds.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 22:30 instructs that the sacrifice of thanksgiving may be eaten on the day of the offering or the next day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:30 states that the sacrifice of thanksgiving must be eaten on the same day and none left until the morrow, forbidding eating it the next day.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 22.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 22:23, what type of offering may be made from a bullock or lamb with a defect if it is a freewill offering?
options: It may be offered and accepted
It may be offered but not accepted for a vow
It may not be offered at all
It may be offered only if the defect is minor
questions.correctAnswer: It may be offered but not accepted for a vow
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:23 states that a bullock or lamb with defects may be offered as a freewill offering but shall not be accepted for a vow offering, highlighting the distinction between freewill and vow offerings.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 22:24 forbid offering unto the LORD?
options: Anything bruised, crushed, broken, or cut
Only animals less than one year old
Only animals not from the tribe of Levi
questions.correctAnswer: Anything bruised, crushed, broken, or cut
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:24 explicitly forbids offering anything bruised, crushed, broken, or cut unto the LORD, emphasizing the demand for perfect offerings.

questions.question: Why shall offerings from a stranger's hand not be accepted according to Leviticus 22:25?
options: Because their corruption and blemishes are in them
Because strangers cannot enter the temple
Because strangers do not understand the laws
questions.correctAnswer: Because their corruption and blemishes are in them
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:25 states that offerings from strangers shall not be accepted because their corruption and blemishes are in them, stressing the importance of purity and sanctity in offerings.

questions.question: How long must a bullock, sheep, or goat be under its mother's care before it is acceptable for a burnt offering?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:27 explains that an animal must be seven days under the dam, and from the eighth day onward it is accepted for an offering made by fire unto the LORD.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 22:28 command regarding killing a cow or ewe and its young?
options: They may be killed on the same day
They shall not be killed both in one day
Only the young may be killed first
Only the mother may be killed first
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not be killed both in one day
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:28 instructs that a cow or ewe and her young shall not be killed both in one day, reflecting concern for mercy and natural order.

questions.question: What instruction is given about eating a sacrifice of thanksgiving in Leviticus 22:30?
options: It may be eaten over several days
It must be eaten on the same day with none left until the morrow
Only the priests may eat it
questions.correctAnswer: It must be eaten on the same day with none left until the morrow
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:30 commands that a sacrifice of thanksgiving shall be eaten on the same day and none shall be left until the next day, emphasizing reverence and prompt consumption.

questions.question: What is the repeated divine self-identification found at the end of Leviticus 22 (verses 31-33), and what does it emphasize?
options: I am the LORD who made heaven and earth
I am the LORD who hallow you and brought you out of Egypt
I am the LORD who judges Israel
I am the LORD who dwells in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: I am the LORD who hallow you and brought you out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:31-33 emphasizes God's identity as the LORD who sanctifies His people and delivered them from Egypt, underscoring His authority and covenant relationship.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of not profaning God's holy name as mentioned in Leviticus 22:32?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 20:7
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:7 commands not to take the LORD's name in vain, echoing the theme in Leviticus 22:32 about not profaning God's holy name.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the principle of offering oneself holy to God, as emphasized in Leviticus 22:31?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 12:1
questions.explanation: Romans 12:1 calls believers to present their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, fulfilling the principle in Leviticus 22:31 about keeping God's commandments and sanctification.

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'blemish' in Leviticus 22:20 refers to a defect or fault making an offering unacceptable?
questions.correctAnswer: Chata’ah
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Chata’ah' (חטאה) denotes a sin or fault, here used for blemish or defect that disqualifies an offering in Leviticus 22:20.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Leviticus 22:31-33 where God repeats 'I am the LORD' multiple times?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:31-33 uses inclusio by repeating 'I am the LORD' at the beginning and end of the passage to frame God's sanctification message.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 22:29, how should a sacrifice of thanksgiving be offered?
questions.correctAnswer: At your own will
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:29 states that thank offerings should be made at one’s own will, indicating voluntary and heartfelt devotion.

questions.question: In Leviticus 22:25, why are offerings from strangers rejected, and how does this relate to the concept of holiness?
options: Strangers are ritually unclean and thus cannot offer sacrifices
Strangers' offerings carry corruption and blemishes, violating holiness
Strangers do not understand the laws, so their offerings are invalid
Strangers are not allowed in the temple courts
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers' offerings carry corruption and blemishes, violating holiness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:25 highlights that the corruption and blemishes in strangers’ offerings render them unacceptable, emphasizing the holiness required in offerings to God.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 22:30 permits leftover thanksgiving sacrifices to be eaten the next day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:30 commands that the thanksgiving sacrifice must be eaten the same day with nothing left for the next day, forbidding leftovers.

questions.question: True or False: Leviticus 22:32 states that God will be hallowed among the children of Israel and commands them not to profane His holy name.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:32 clearly commands that God's holy name not be profaned and that He will be hallowed among Israel, emphasizing sanctification.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is emphasized in Leviticus 22:2 when God commands Aaron and his sons to separate themselves from the holy things?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:2 states that Aaron and his sons must separate themselves from the holy things so as not to profane God's holy name, demonstrating God's attribute of holiness.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 22:4, what condition disqualifies a man of Aaron's seed from eating the holy things until he is clean?
options: Leprosy or having a running issue
questions.correctAnswer: Leprosy or having a running issue
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:4 specifically prohibits any man of Aaron's seed who is a leper or has a running issue from eating the holy things until he is clean.

questions.question: What consequence does Leviticus 22:3 prescribe for anyone with uncleanness who approaches the holy things?
options: That soul shall be cut off from God's presence
They shall offer a sin offering
They shall be excommunicated for seven days
They shall bring a burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: That soul shall be cut off from God's presence
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:3 warns that anyone of Aaron's seed who has uncleanness upon him and goes to the holy things shall be cut off from the LORD's presence.

questions.question: What theological principle is taught by Leviticus 22:8 regarding eating animals that die of themselves or are torn by beasts?
options: Encouragement to trust God for provision
Allowance if the animal is clean
questions.correctAnswer: Prohibition to avoid defilement
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:8 forbids eating animals that die of themselves or are torn by beasts to prevent defilement, teaching God's demand for purity.

questions.question: Leviticus 22:10 forbids which group from eating the holy thing?
options: Strangers, sojourners of the priest, or hired servants
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers, sojourners of the priest, or hired servants
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:10 clearly states that no stranger, sojourner of the priest, or hired servant shall eat of the holy thing.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by the requirement in Leviticus 22:19-20 that offerings be without blemish?
options: The doctrine of sacrificial purity and perfection
The doctrine of grace through imperfect offerings
The doctrine of fasting before offering
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of sacrificial purity and perfection
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:19-20 commands that offerings be a male without blemish, teaching the doctrine that sacrifices must be pure and perfect to be acceptable to God.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 22:26-27 contribute to the biblical narrative of redemption regarding the preparation of offerings?
options: It shows God's concern for proper timing and sanctity in worship
It teaches that any animal can be offered at any time
It allows offerings of animals under one day old
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's concern for proper timing and sanctity in worship
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:26-27 prescribes that a young animal shall be under its dam for seven days before offering, underscoring God's holiness and order in the redemptive worship process.

questions.question: What synthesis of teaching is conveyed by Leviticus 22:5-6 and 22:11 about uncleanness and eating of holy things?
options: Those unclean must purify themselves to partake, but those bought by a priest may eat
All Israelites may eat holy things regardless of uncleanness
Only Aaron's sons may eat the holy things
questions.correctAnswer: Those unclean must purify themselves to partake, but those bought by a priest may eat
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:5-6 require washing to become clean before eating holy things, while 22:11 allows priests to feed those they buy, showing purity's importance and the priest's authority.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining Leviticus 22:15-16 regarding profaning holy things and bearing iniquity?
options: Profaning holy things causes sin and guilt to be borne
Holy things can be profaned without consequence
Only non-priests can profane holy things
Profaning holy things results in immediate death without sin
questions.correctAnswer: Profaning holy things causes sin and guilt to be borne
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:15-16 warns that profaning holy things leads to bearing sin and guilt, teaching the seriousness of sanctity and God's sanctifying work.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 22:31-32 teach about the relationship between God's commandments and His holy name?
options: Obedience preserves God's holiness and prevents profaning His name
God's name can be profaned without consequence
Profaning God's name is unrelated to obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience preserves God's holiness and prevents profaning His name
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:31-32 commands keeping God's commandments to avoid profaning His holy name and to be holy as He is holy.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 22:29-30, what is required when offering a sacrifice of thanksgiving to the LORD?
options: It must be eaten the same day, leaving none until the morning
It must be offered only by priests
It must be burnt entirely on the altar
questions.correctAnswer: It must be eaten the same day, leaving none until the morning
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:29-30 instructs that thanksgiving sacrifices be eaten the same day to honor the LORD properly without defilement.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the strict purity laws in Leviticus 22 are arbitrary and irrelevant today. What does Leviticus 22:1-3 and 22:32-33 actually teach about God's purpose for these laws?
options: These laws reveal God's holiness and His desire to sanctify His people
These laws are merely cultural and have no divine authority
They are only about hygiene and public health
They were designed to exclude outsiders unfairly
questions.correctAnswer: These laws reveal God's holiness and His desire to sanctify His people
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:1-3 and 32-33 emphasize God's holiness and sanctification of Israel, showing these laws are divine mandates to preserve His holy name and people.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 22:12-13 teach theologically about the status of a priest's daughter married to a stranger versus a widow or divorced daughter returned to her father's house?
options: Marriage to a stranger disqualifies her from holy offerings, but return to her father's house restores her right
Both married daughters and widows may eat of holy things freely
Only widows are excluded from eating holy things
Marriage status has no bearing on eating holy things
questions.correctAnswer: Marriage to a stranger disqualifies her from holy offerings, but return to her father's house restores her right
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:12-13 sets a distinction based on marital status and household, showing how covenantal belonging affects participation in holy offerings.

questions.question: What doctrinal principle is highlighted by Leviticus 22:14 concerning unintentional consumption of holy things?
options: Restitution plus a fifth must be added to the offering
No penalty is required for unintentional consumption
The holy thing must be burnt immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Restitution plus a fifth must be added to the offering
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:14 requires adding a fifth part to the holy thing if eaten unwittingly, teaching accountability even for unintentional sins.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in Leviticus 22:33 where He identifies Himself as the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness as Redeemer
questions.explanation: Leviticus 22:33 reveals God's faithfulness by recalling His deliverance of Israel from Egypt, emphasizing His redeeming character.
